display.purpose: Page titles and session headings. Used once per screen, never in repeating components.

headline.purpose: Card headings, section headings within feedback view, scenario titles.

title.purpose: Sidebar nav labels, form section headings, rubric dimension names.

body.purpose: All prose — feedback summary, scenario context, growth area descriptions. Max 65–72ch.

label.purpose: Badges, timestamps, dimension score labels, metadata, form labels. Never uppercase-tracked eyebrows.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Applied on hover to interactive session history cards alongside Studio Warm background shift. Not used at rest.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Reserved for dropdown menus, command palette, and overlaid panels. Never on static content.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state changes: hover, focus, active. Background, border-color, box-shadow.

motion.name: recording-pulse
motion.purpose: Recording state indicator dot only. The only continuous animation in the product.

narrative.overview:
The room before the recording booth. Warm, quiet, prepared — the kind of space that puts you at ease before the work begins. Voxara's interface occupies the same register: it creates the conditions for a real coaching experience and makes you want to be here. When a student sees their feedback, the UI should feel like someone who genuinely cares sat down with them, pointed at specific moments, and said exactly what to try next.

Color is restrained and purposeful. Warmth comes from the amber that runs through the surfaces — not from decoration, but from the material quality of the space itself. A deep warm crimson anchors the identity on primary actions. The surface is a warm near-white that has genuine presence without weight. Every screen has one job; none of them feel like work.

References: Notion (information with typographic care), Pitch (focused creative-professional, generous spacing), Are.na (calm, open, non-institutional). All three feel like spaces, not tools.
keyCharacteristics: Warm without being cozy: inviting, not casual
Craft-focused: the UI signals that what you're doing here is serious and worth your time
Light and open: no visual weight that competes with the work
Coaching-toned: the vocabulary of the UI matches the vocabulary of a supportive coach
Restrained motion that communicates state, not decoration

rules.name: The Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Studio Crimson appears on ≤15% of any given screen. It marks the single most important interactive moment — the recording button, the primary CTA, the active sidebar item. When everything is red, nothing is. Reserve it, and it earns its weight.

rules.name: The Warmth Rule
rules.body: Structural warmth comes from Coaching Amber and Studio Warm, not from the surface tint alone. When a card or nav item is hovered or active, it should warm — not just darken or shadow. Warmth is the primary interactivity signal; shadow is secondary.

rules.name: The Light-Is-The-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stay light. The warmth is in the character of the light, not in reducing it. Dark surfaces belong to a different product.

rules.name: The No Blue-Purple Rule
rules.body: No blue, indigo, or purple in the palette. These are the generic tech defaults and contradict the creative-professional character Voxara is building.

rules.name: The Single Family Rule
rules.body: Plus Jakarta Sans only. No display font pairings, no serif headings for character. Brand character comes from the crimson and the quality of information hierarchy — not from typographic mixing.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Small all-caps tracked labels above every section heading are prohibited. They read as AI scaffold. Section names live in the heading hierarchy itself, or are simply absent when context is established by navigation.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Elements are flat at rest. Shadow appears only as a response to state (hover on interactive cards) or structural float (dropdowns, overlays).

rules.name: The Warmth-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: When signaling interactivity on hover, shift background to Studio Warm first. Add Float shadow if additional depth is needed. Warmth is the primary signal; shadow is the secondary.

dos: Do use Studio Crimson only on primary interactive moments: the record button, primary CTA, active nav indicator. Its scarcity is what makes it mean something.
Do use Studio Warm as the primary hover/active signal on cards and sidebar items. Warmth communicates interactivity before any other visual change.
Do let Coaching Amber carry structural warmth beyond badges — hover tints, active section backgrounds, score pips. It is the warmth of the room, not just a data color.
Do present feedback in a clear visual hierarchy: summary → dimension scores → strengths → growth areas.
Do use tonal layering (Canvas → Studio Surface → Studio Warm) to define layers and states rather than shadows.
Do give every interactive component its full state vocabulary: default, hover, focus, active, disabled.
Do keep body text at Ink (oklch(0.15 0.025 27)) on Canvas backgrounds. Muted text is for secondary information only.
Do write UI copy in the coaching register: direct, specific, encouraging.
Do keep transitions at 150–250ms with ease-out curves.
donts: Don't use pure white (oklch(1.000 0.000 0)) for Canvas. The warmth requires the amber tilt.
Don't use Studio Warm for text or borders. Background-only.
Don't use enterprise SaaS patterns: dashboard hero metrics, feature grids, navy-and-blue palettes, corporate tone.
Don't use gamification UI (streaks, XP bars, confetti). Voxara is serious skill development.
Don't use a dark/gothic aesthetic. The brief explicitly excludes it.
Don't use blue or purple anywhere in the palette.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Single solid color only.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px as colored accent).
Don't write vague feedback UI copy. Every piece of text should name a moment, quote a phrase, give a timestamp.
Don't use motion for decoration. The only continuous animation is the recording pulse.
Don't build modal-first flows. Inline or separate screens instead.
